title: Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight
why: Introduces CAPA, a chance-adjusted functional-similarity metric showing models think alike (correlated mistakes) as they improve, undermining LLM-as-judge/weak-to-strong oversight; the digest.md N3 baseline for single-snapshot cross-model functional similarity that this paper extends to a longitudinal, cross-vendor drift-vector design. Sourced from topics/corpus/ideas.jsonl (proposal-level record, no cached PDF) -- added here to satisfy goal.md Phase A cache-integrity (every N3 key must be a selected cache record).

title: Cultivating Pluralism In Algorithmic Monoculture: The Community Alignment Dataset
why: Names and mitigates "algorithmic monoculture": RLHF/DPO candidates sampled from models sharing training data/architecture occupy a narrow response-space region; a concrete within-pipeline mechanism this paper generalizes to across-vendor drift synchrony. digest.md N3 method-twin.

title: What happens when generative AI models train recursively on each others' outputs?
why: Models multi-entity recursive training on a shared pool of AI-generated web text and characterizes when this drives convergence toward homogeneous behavior across models -- a concrete cross-model homogenization mechanism, but validated in controlled/simulated training rather than by auditing deployed multi-vendor version sequences. digest.md N3 method-twin.

title: Diversity-Aware Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Reasoning
why: Documents that RL post-training (RLHF, GRPO) systematically collapses a single model's output diversity even as accuracy improves; relevant structural analog for the diversity-collapse mechanism but characterizes one model's own distribution, not cross-vendor convergence. digest.md N4 limitation target.

title: Post-training Large Language Models for Diverse High-Quality Responses
why: Shows RLHF/GRPO concentrate probability mass on a narrow set of canonical responses (mode collapse) and proposes a diversity-quality optimization objective; same RL-diversity-collapse mechanism as DiversityAwarePO, at the single-model level, not cross-vendor. digest.md N4 limitation target.

title: Measurement-theoretic framework for dataset diversity as a latent construct (Zhao, Andrews, Papakyriakopoulos, Xiang)
why: Provides a measurement-theoretic framework (conceptualize -> operationalize -> validate reliability/validity) for treating "diversity" as a latent construct; a structural exemplar this paper follows so its own behavioral-diversity index is defensible rather than ad hoc, per guidance.md Part 5 / Part 2-A2 R2. Aimed at dataset construction, not deployed-model behavior, hence background rather than method-twin.

title: A Closer Look at Model Collapse: From a Generalization-to-Memorization Perspective
why: Analyzes model collapse under recursive training on synthetic data through a generalization-to-memorization lens, explaining sharp diversity/quality degradation that slow asymptotic-variance accounts miss; theoretical mechanism for why shared synthetic data could rapidly narrow behavior, validated on toy/single-family models rather than real multi-vendor releases. digest.md N4 limitation target.

title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
why: ICML 2025 large-scale audit (350+ LLMs) finding substantial cross-model error correlation with provider/architecture as explicit factors and, crucially, that more accurate models err together even across distinct vendors -- the strongest published snapshot form of this paper's capability-attractor confound, and the deployment stakes (LLM-as-judge, hiring/monoculture) match this paper's motivation; no temporal axis, which is the delta this paper adds.

title: Are LLMs becoming similarly creative? Evidence from three years of models
why: Contemporaneous (2026-08-19) preliminary analysis reporting a statistically significant decline in cross-model output diversity over three years of releases (sentence-embedding similarity on Infinity-Chat100 + Alternate Uses Task) -- the first longitudinal cross-model diversity-trend evidence, partially scooping RQ6's direction; pooled across models (no per-vendor panels), single embedding index (no two-index gate, no noise floor), and no drift-vector correlation or capability control -- the deltas this paper's concede-and-claim paragraph states.

title: The Vendi Score: A Diversity Evaluation Metric for Machine Learning
why: Source of the Vendi Score, this paper's primary diversity index (Two-Index Diversity Trend / RQ6); previously used in the draft without citation -- instrument-credit fix from review_2026-08.
